runs.t: •  Say the days of the week.

slides.notes:
Welcome. Say: "Today: time and days." Point to the clock: "What time is it?"
Bring a clock you can move. A paper plate with two paper hands and a pin works well. Teach :00 and :30 first, then :15 and :45.
Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Say less, show more.
Class plan: 6:00 Hello + Review, 6:10 New Words, 6:20 Listening, 6:32 Grammar, 6:45 Break, 7:00 Talk Time, 7:10 Exit Ticket + Homework, 7:15 Letters & Numbers, 7:25 Progress Check.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (At a glance, How to Use This Plan, Clock-time plan).

slides.title: What Time Is It?

runs.t: I can ask and tell the time.
I can say the days of the week.
I can use at 6:00, on Monday, in the morning.
I can ask: Is it open on Sunday?
I can say when I work.

slides.notes:
Click to show each goal, one at a time. Read it aloud. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: move the class clock. "What time is it?" "It's six thirty."
Goal 3: at + a time (at 6:00), on + a day (on Monday), in + the morning.
Goal 5: learners who don't work can say: "English class is on Monday, at 6:00."
Letters & Numbers at 7:15: writing times, short day names (Mon., Tue.), and a store-hours sign.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (At a glance: Objectives).
slides.title: Today's Goals

runs.t: A: Do you work at night?

slides.notes:
Pairs. Review of last week (jobs). 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
Before class, write on the board: What do you do? Where do you work? Do you work at night? and the 3 "everyone" answers: I'm a student. I'm a homemaker. I don't work now.
Model with one learner: "What do you do?" "I'm a cashier." "Where do you work?" "I work at a store."
Click to show the A question. Click again for the B answers. Partners switch, then find a new partner. Help: "Can you repeat, please?" "How do you spell it?"
Last 3 minutes: homework check. Partners show each other the Lesson 5 homework. Look at item 2 (a / an).
New learners: pair them with a strong partner. If behind: one partner only.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Step 1: Hello + Review; Student Pages: Hello + Review).

slides.notes:
Show the class clock. Set it to 9:00: "What time is it? It's nine o'clock." Move it to 9:30: "It's nine thirty." Write on the board: 9:00 = nine o'clock, 9:30 = nine thirty = half past nine.
Click to show each picture. Point and say the word. Learners repeat 2 times.
morning / afternoon / evening: move your arm like the sun (low, high, gone).
Say "It's six o'clock", never "They are six".
★ = most important words. If behind: teach :00 and :30 only.

slides.title: More New Words

runs.t: Kim calls a laundromat. Then she calls a school.
What time is the English class?
Is the school open on Friday?

slides.notes:
Before you listen (1 min). Say: "Kim calls a laundromat." Mime washing clothes. "She hears a message. Then she calls a school." Hold up your phone.
Click to show each listen. Listen 1: Task A (circle the time). Listen 2: Task B (check the days). Listen 3: Task C (write the times and the word).
Say it!: read each line. Learners repeat.
The audio L1_L6_listening.mp3 (about 1:00) plays the message and the call once. Press play again for the next listen. Pairs compare after each task.
No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer (one person reads the message and the receptionist; the other reads Kim).
Voices: Narrator, store message, Receptionist, Kim. Synthetic voices made with Chatterbox TTS (MIT), copied from short reference clips made with Kokoro-82M (Apache 2.0); no recordings of real people.

slides.title: Before You Listen

runs.t: Kim calls a laundromat and a school.

slides.notes:
Listen 1 (Task A). Learners circle one time on each line.
Pairs compare: "Show your partner." Then click to show each answer: 1 7:00, 2 9:00, 3 6:00.
The message: open Monday to Saturday, from seven in the morning to nine at night. The English class is at six o'clock.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Step 3: Listening; Student Pages: Listening A; Answer key, Listening Task A).
slides.title: Listening A

runs.t: Listen again. Check the days. Write.
B: the days.  C: the times and a word.
C. On Friday, the school is

slides.notes:
Listen 2 (Task B): learners check the days on their page. Listen 3 (Task C): learners write the times and the word.
Pairs compare. Then click to show each answer.
Task B: the laundromat is open Mon., Tue., Wed., Thu., Fri., Sat. (not Sun.). The English class is on Mon. and Wed.
Task C: 1 from 9:00 to 3:00, 2 weekend.
If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Step 3: Listening; Answer key, Listening Tasks B and C).
slides.title: Listening B + C

slides.notes:
Show the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer. Point left, then right.
Move the class clock: 6:00, 6:30, 6:15, 6:45. Ask "What time is it?" The class answers "It's…" each time. Click to show each answer.
Teach :00 and :30 first. :15 and :45 are said as numbers: six fifteen, six forty-five. (Quarter past / quarter to is Level 2; accept it if a learner knows it.)
The big mistake: "They are six." In English: It's six o'clock. Tap the clock: "It's six."
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Box 1; Teacher notes).

slides.title: What time is it?

slides.notes:
Draw 3 boxes on the board: at 6:00 (a clock), on Monday (a calendar), in the morning (a sun).
Ask: "What time is class?" Click: "It's at 6:00." Say: "at + time."
Ask: "What day is class?" Click: "It's on Monday." Say: "on + day." Say on Monday, not the Monday.
Check questions: "Class is ___ 6:00." (at) "Class is ___ Monday." (on)
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Boxes 2 and 4; Grammar Box 2; Teacher notes).
Pictures: Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc. and other contributors (https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); resized and combined with drawn parts (see lesson6/images/CREDITS.md).
slides.title: What time is class?

slides.notes:
Box 3: ask "When do you work?" Click: "On Monday and Tuesday. In the morning."
Learners who don't work: "When is English class?" Click: "On Monday, at 6:00."
Box 4 (top right): at + a time, on + a day, in + the morning / the afternoon / the evening. Say once: at night (not in the night).
Check question: "I work ___ the morning." (in)
Don't ask about real work hours if a learner doesn't offer them. "English class is on Monday at 6:00" is always a good answer.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Boxes 3 and 4; Teacher notes).
slides.title: When do you work?

runs.t: Is the store open on Sunday?

slides.notes:
Point to the CLOSED sign: "Is the store open on Sunday?" Click: "No, it isn't. It's closed."
Right box: "Is it open on Monday?" "What time is it open?" Click: "Yes, it is. From 9:00 to 5:00."
Say closed, not close: "The store is closed."
Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks from the left side of the Grammar page; B answers from the right side. Then switch.
If behind: skip the pair drill. It becomes homework, and Talk Time practices the same questions.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Box 5; pair drill).

slides.title: Grammar Box 5

slides.notes:
Learners write at, on, or in on each line. Then pairs check.
Click to show each answer: 1 at, 2 on, 3 in, 4 at, 5 on.
Say: "at + time. on + day. in + the morning." Line 4 is the exception: at night.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Grammar: Practice; Answer key, Grammar practice).
slides.title: at, on, in?

slides.notes:
Read each "Don't say" line. Shake your head. Click to show the correct line. Learners repeat it.
The big mistake this week: "They are six." Spanish says "Son las seis." In English: It's six o'clock. Tap the clock: "It's six."
at 6:00, on Monday (not the Monday), in the morning, but at night.
Days always start with a capital letter: Monday. Say closed, not close.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Grammar: Common mistakes; Teacher notes).

slides.title: Common Mistakes

runs.t: Is the library open on Monday?
Yes, it is. / No, it isn't.
A asks: What time is it open?

slides.notes:
A–B pairs. Give half the class the Student A page and half the Student B page. Partners don't show their pages.
Model with one learner (you are A): "Is the library open on Monday?" "No, it isn't." "Is it open on Tuesday?" "Yes, it is." "What time is it open?" "From 10:00 to 6:00." Write it in an empty table on the board.
Click to show each step. Part 1 (6 min): A asks about B's 3 places and writes the days and times. Then B asks about A's places. Check (1 min): partners show their pages and compare.
Answer key: Clinic Mon.–Fri. 8:00–5:00. Store every day 7:00–10:00. Laundromat Mon.–Sat. 6:00–9:00. Library Tue.–Sat. 10:00–6:00. Restaurant every day 11:00–9:00. Bank Mon.–Fri. 9:00–4:00.
With an odd number, two Bs share one A. Learners who can't read or write yet ask the questions while a partner writes, or they point to the days.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Step 5: Talk Time, Part 1; Student Pages: Talk Time A and B; Answer key).

slides.title: Talk Time

runs.t: I don't work now. English class is

slides.notes:
Part 2 (3 min). New question: "When do you work?" (or "When do you study? When is English class?").
Model it: "When do you work?" Click: "On Monday and Friday, in the morning."
Each learner says one sentence: "I work on Monday and Friday, in the morning." / "I don't work now. English class is on ___, at 6:00."
Strong learners can add from… to…: "I work from 8:00 to 4:00." Don't ask about real hours if a learner doesn't offer them.
If behind: skip Part 2.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Step 5: Talk Time, Part 2; Teacher notes).
slides.title: When Do You Work?

slides.notes:
Exit ticket (never skip): set the class clock to a time. Each learner says the time ("It's seven fifteen.") or writes one sentence: Class is on ___, at ___. Copying is fine.
Homework (10 minutes): open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (the first line). Point to each instruction.
Homework: 1) English class is on ___, at ___. I work on ___ (or I don't work now); 2) at, on, or in; 3) write the time with numbers; 4) ask a family member or a friend 3 times: What time is it?; 5) review: I'm a / an ___ (or My mother is a / an ___).
Homework answers: item 2: 1 on, 2 at, 3 in, 4 on, 5 at. Item 3: 1 7:00, 2 8:30, 3 4:15, 4 5:45.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Step 6: Exit Ticket + Homework; Student Pages: Homework; Answer key).

slides.title: Before You Go

slides.notes:
Letters & Numbers (10 min). Whole class, then pairs. Use the Letters & Numbers page.
Task A (2 min): point to each clock. Say: six o'clock, six fifteen, six thirty, six forty-five. Learners repeat. Click to show each time.
Show the : (two dots) between the hour and the minutes.
7:15 and 7:50 sound alike. Say "fif-TEEN" and "FIF-ty" with a clap, as in Lesson 3.
Learners who can't read or write yet: they say the times with everyone and point to the clocks.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Letters & Numbers, Task A; Teacher notes).

slides.title: Letters & Numbers: Task A

slides.notes:
Task B (3 min). Say each time 2 times: 1 7:30, 2 8:00, 3 9:15, 4 10:45. Learners write them with numbers.
Then click to show each answer.
Partners: A says a time, B writes it. Switch.
If behind: do Tasks A and B only.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Letters & Numbers, Task B; Answer key, Letters & Numbers Task B).
slides.title: Write the Time

slides.notes:
Task C (2 min). Days start with a capital letter: Monday. The short form is 3 letters + a period: Mon.
Read each day. Learners repeat. Click to show each short form: Mon., Tue., Wed., Thu., Fri., Sat., Sun. Learners write them.
AM / PM: say once on the next slide. Signs use them; learners don't need to say them.
Learners who can't read or write yet: in Task C they copy Mon. and Sat. only. A helper, if you have one, sits with them.

The store is open on Sunday.

slides.notes:
Task D (2 min). Read the sign together. Say: "AM = morning. PM = afternoon and night."
Read each line. Learners circle Yes or No and write the time. Then click to show each answer: 1 Yes, 2 No, 3 9:00 (9 AM) to 5:00 (5 PM).

slides.title: Read the Sign

runs.t: 3. Is the bank open on Sunday?
d. No, it isn't. It's closed.

slides.notes:
Progress Check (5 min). Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read the 5 times slowly, 2 times each: 1 6:30, 2 7:15, 3 3:00, 4 9:45, 5 11:30. Learners circle.
Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Help with the instructions only. Click to show the Part B answers when you check together: 1 c, 2 a, 3 d, 4 b.
Part C answers: 1 at, 2 on, 3 in.
Part D: read each "I can…" line and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "A little." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
Score: A /5 + B /4 + C /3 = /12. This is not a test grade. Part A shows who can hear times; Part C shows at / on / in. Collect the pages. If behind: do it in Week 7 at 6:00, while learners arrive.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson6/Level1_Lesson6.md (Progress Check; Answer key).
